sections.h2: Notice rules depend on the city or county
sections.html:
Kentucky has no single statewide notice code for residential rentals. KRS 383.500 lets cities, counties and urban-county governments adopt the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, KRS 383.505 to 383.715, but only as a whole and without amendment. The act's notice periods bind only the places that did so.

A number of places have adopted it, including 33 cities counted in a 2017 fiscal note. Louisville, Lexington, Covington, Newport and Florence are among them, as are Oldham County and Pulaski County. Plenty of other towns have not. Phone the clerk for the town or county that holds the house before you pick a notice form.

The table lines up each situation with its period and its statute. Where a row says URLTA, the period applies only in a place that adopted the act.

sections.h2: Overdue rent in a URLTA place
sections.html:
The tenant gets a week, counted from the landlord's written notice. The notice must say that rent is late and that the landlord intends to end the tenancy if the money does not arrive. A tenant who pays inside that week removes the ground to terminate.

Taking money can undo the notice. Under KRS 383.675, accepting rent with knowledge of the default, or accepting performance that varies from the agreement, waives the right to end the tenancy for that breach unless the parties later agree otherwise. An owner lining up a sale should decide early whether part-payments will be taken.

sections.h2: When the problem is a lease violation, not money
sections.html:
In a URLTA place, the landlord serves a notice that names the acts or omissions and picks an end date at least 14 days after the tenant receives it. If the breach is still open on day 15, the agreement ends as the notice says.

  • A repairable breach is cured if the tenant repairs it or pays for it before the stated end date, and then the agreement continues.
  • The same conduct returning within six months lets the landlord end the agreement on a new 14-day notice with no chance to cure.
  • A tenant who stays on in bad faith after termination risks a judgment for the larger of three months' periodic rent or triple the actual damages, with reasonable lawyer fees added.

KRS 383.535 lists arrangements the act does not govern, and notices for these follow other rules. Check the list before using a notice form meant for an ordinary apartment lease.

  • Residence at a care, detention or counseling institution when incidental to that service.
  • Occupancy by a buyer under a contract of sale, or by a person who takes over that buyer's interest.
  • Members living in a fraternal or social organization's quarters.
  • Transient stays in a hotel or motel.
  • An employee whose right to live there depends on the job.
  • Condominium owners and cooperative proprietary lease holders.
  • A dwelling on land used for livestock, poultry or crops, including tobacco and timber.

sections.h2: Older rules where the act has not been adopted
sections.html:
Chapter 383's older sections take over. A tenancy at will or by sufferance ends on one month's written notice to remove, and a fixed term simply expires on its date.

A tenant who stays after the term gains no right to remain for 90 days when the term was a year or longer, and for 30 days when it was shorter, and the landlord can start the court case inside those periods without demand or notice. Wait past them and no case can start until a full year (or 60 days, for a shorter term) goes by after the term ends. A city or county cannot pass an ordinance on the subjects the act covers, though ordinances on other housing matters can exist.

sections.h2: How to deliver a Kentucky eviction notice
sections.html:
A tenant receives notice when it is handed over or sent by registered or certified letter to the address the tenant gave for communications, or to the last known home if none was given. A landlord receives notice by a written delivery to the business address used for the rental, or by certified letter there.

Keep a copy, the mailing slip and a dated note of who delivered what. Receipt starts the 14-day count, so mail should leave early enough that the end date still works.

In a URLTA place, KRS 383.695 gives the tenant the same periods the landlord has: seven days for week-to-week, 30 days before the rental date for month-to-month, and 10 days for a tenancy that began when a written lease ended.

A tenant's own notice can empty a house before listing with no court case at all. File it with its date and confirm the move-out date in writing.

sections.h2: What a landlord may not do while a notice runs
sections.html:
A landlord may not take possession by self-help. KRS 383.690 bars regaining the unit by action or otherwise, including shutting off heat, electric power, running water, hot water, gas or another essential service, except for abandonment, surrender or as the act allows.

Retaliation is barred too. After a tenant complains to a code agency, complains to the landlord about a covered violation or joins a tenant group, KRS 383.705 forbids rent hikes, service cuts and threatened possession suits. A complaint made in the prior year creates a presumption of retaliation, yet the landlord may still sue when the tenant is behind on rent.

sections.h2: How a notice interacts with selling the rented house
sections.html:
Closing on the house does not by itself end the tenancy. Under KRS 383.600, a seller who conveys in a good faith sale to a bona fide purchaser is freed from liability under the rental agreement for events that follow the tenant's written notice of the conveyance, absent a contrary agreement.

Showings need lead time. KRS 383.615 calls for two days' notice before the landlord enters to display the unit to prospective buyers, at reasonable hours, with emergencies excepted, and a tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry.

  • Decide whether to list with the tenant living there or finish the notice first.
  • Send the tenant written word of the sale once a contract is signed.
  • Ask the closing attorney who will hold the security deposit. KRS 383.580 requires deposits to sit in a separate account and requires damage listings at move-in and move-out.

If the buyer wants the house empty, work backward from the closing date. A 30-day month-to-month notice has to be delivered a full 30 days before the next rent date, and a notice for a lease violation needs at least 14 days after receipt. Build in the days it takes to mail and receive the paper.

faqs.q: What notice must a landlord give for unpaid rent in Kentucky?
faqs.a: Seven days where the URLTA is in force. The landlord gives written word that rent is overdue and that the tenancy will end, and the tenant has a week to pay.

faqs.q: How does a month-to-month tenancy end in Kentucky?
faqs.a: Written notice delivered 30 days before the date rent is next due, from either side, under KRS 383.695(2). Outside URLTA places, one month's written notice ends a tenancy at will.

faqs.q: Can a Kentucky landlord evict with no notice at all?
faqs.a: Only in a narrow case. When a tenancy continues after a written lease and the rent is 10 days late, KRS 383.695(3) lets the landlord end it without notice. Otherwise a written notice comes first.

faqs.q: Can an owner shut off utilities or change locks to push a tenant out?
faqs.a: No. KRS 383.690 forbids recovering possession by interrupting heat, power, water, gas or another essential service. Possession comes through a court order.

faqs.q: Does a sale of the house cancel the lease?
faqs.a: Not by itself. KRS 383.600 only relieves the seller of liability for later events once the tenant has written notice of the conveyance. Read the lease and the sale contract for the rest.
